name: Standing hip CARs
description: Controlled Articular Rotations for the hip — the widest possible active circle the hip can own, one leg at a time. Active mobility, not a passive stretch.
setup: Stand tall on one leg, hand on a wall for balance
Drive the other knee up to the front as high as it will actively go
Take that knee out to the side, then rotate the hip so the heel sweeps back
Extend the leg behind, then reverse the circle
cues: Move the hip, not the spine — ribs stay stacked over pelvis, no arching
Go slow at the edges of the circle; that end-range is where the work is
Own the range actively; don't fling the leg

name: 90/90 hip switch
description: Seated 90/90 rotations train hip internal and external rotation together — the exact range that limits cutting and change of direction.
setup: Sit with front leg bent 90° in front, back leg bent 90° out to the side
Keep the chest tall and both sit-bones as heavy as you can
Rotate both knees over to the other side, lifting through the hips
Pause when the trailing knee lifts — that's your internal-rotation edge
cues: Internal rotation is the goal — the trailing hip that wants to lift
Hinge forward over the front shin for a deeper external-rotation load
Slow and controlled; no bouncing

name: Cossack squat (active)
description: Wide lateral squat that opens the adductors and loads one hip deep while the other leg extends — mobility trained under your own control.
setup: Stand wide, feet a little turned out
Shift into one hip, sitting deep, keeping that whole foot down
The other leg stays long, toes up
Pause at the bottom, then shift smoothly to the other side
cues: Keep the working heel planted — no rolling onto the toes
Knee tracks over the foot, never caving in
Own a brief pause at the bottom rather than bouncing through

name: World's greatest stretch
description: A moving lunge-plus-rotation that hits the hip flexor, adductor, and thoracic rotation in one active flow. Prime, don't stretch-and-hold.
setup: Step into a long lunge, both hands inside the front foot
Drop the back knee slightly to feel the hip flexor lengthen
Drive the inside elbow toward the floor, then rotate that arm up to the ceiling
Follow the hand with the eyes, then switch sides
cues: Rotate from the mid-back, opening the chest
Keep the front knee tracking over the foot
Move continuously — this is a prep flow, not a static hold

name: Knee-to-wall ankle rock
description: Loaded ankle dorsiflexion mobilization. Restricted dorsiflexion drives the knee inward on every squat, land, and cut — free it at the base.
setup: Face a wall in a half-kneel, front foot a few inches back from it
Drive the front knee forward over the toes to touch the wall — heel stays down
If it touches easily, slide the foot back and repeat at the new distance
Rock in and out at your end range
cues: Heel must stay glued to the floor — that's the honest range
Knee travels straight over the 2nd/3rd toe, not inward
Small, repeated rocks into the end range

name: Deep squat sit
description: Sitting in the bottom of a deep squat and actively organizing it — ankles, hips, and pelvis learning to own end-range under body weight.
setup: Squat down as far as is comfortable, heels down, holding something in front if needed
Let the hips sink between the feet
Gently press the knees out with the elbows and lift the chest
Shift side to side and rock the ankles to explore the position
cues: Heels stay down; widen the stance if they lift
Actively press knees out — don't just hang passively
Breathe into the position and relax the hips lower

name: Short-foot / tripod
description: Actively doming the arch by drawing the ball of the foot toward the heel without curling the toes. Wakes the intrinsic foot muscles — the base of the whole chain.
setup: Stand with the foot flat, weight through the tripod: big-toe ball, little-toe ball, heel
Without curling the toes, draw the ball of the foot toward the heel so the arch lifts
Hold the dome, toes long and relaxed
Release slowly
cues: Toes stay long and flat — the lift comes from under the arch
Keep all three tripod points loaded
Small movement, big focus

name: Windlass big-toe press
description: Driving the big toe down (or extending it) to tension the plantar fascia and raise the arch — the windlass mechanism, the foot's own spring and the start of the foot→glute line.
setup: Stand with the foot in its tripod
Press the big toe firmly into the floor while keeping the other toes relaxed
Feel the arch rise and the plantar fascia tension
Alternate: lift and spread the toes, then set just the big toe back down first
cues: Big toe drives down, arch lifts — that's the spring loading
Don't let the arch collapse inward
Keep the heel and outer foot quiet

name: Hyperarch hold
description: Tensioning the whole foot into a locked, high-arch spring and holding it — not curling the toes, but drawing the forefoot and heel toward each other so the arch domes and the ankle stiffens as one unit. The foot-first connection the rest of the chain hangs from (HFT-inspired: train tension, not isolated toes).
setup: Stand barefoot in the tripod: big-toe ball, little-toe ball, and heel all loaded
Without clawing the toes, draw the forefoot and heel toward each other so the arch lifts and locks
Feel the whole foot and ankle stiffen into one springy unit, toes long and relaxed
Hold the tension, breathing easy; release slowly
cues: Lock the whole foot as ONE unit — this is tension, not a toe curl
Big-toe ball stays planted as the arch domes up
The ankle stiffens with the arch — one connected spring from the ground up

name: Single-leg calf isometric
description: A mid-range single-leg heel-raise hold. Builds ankle and Achilles stiffness — the stored spring you need before any hopping.
setup: Stand on one foot, fingertips on a wall for balance
Rise onto the ball of the foot to a strong mid-height position
Hold rock-steady, ankle stacked over the foot
Lower under control
cues: Push evenly through the big-toe and little-toe balls — no rolling out
Ankle doesn't wobble; build a stiff, quiet spring
Keep the arch locked (hyperarch) as you rise — carry the foot tension up the leg
Tall through the whole leg

name: Tibialis raise
description: Pulling the toes up against gravity to train the front of the shin — the balancing partner to the calf and a key brake for deceleration.
setup: Stand with the back against a wall, heels a step out from it
Keep the legs straight and lean the hips back on the wall
Pull the toes and forefoot up toward the shins as high as possible
Lower slowly under control
cues: Heels stay planted; only the forefoot lifts
Feel the burn on the front of the shin
Control the way down — don't drop

name: Banded ankle in/eversion
description: Light-band resisted ankle turns for the sides of the ankle — the stabilizers that keep the ankle honest on quick direction changes.
setup: Sit with the leg out, band looped around the forefoot and anchored to the side
Turn the sole outward against the band (eversion), then reset
Re-anchor on the other side and turn the sole inward (inversion)
Move only at the ankle
cues: Slow and deliberate — the light band is for control, not load
Keep the shin still; the motion is all foot
Full range both directions

name: Single-leg balance (quiet foot)
description: Standing on one foot and making the foot and ankle go quiet. Trains the sensory side of the base — the foot learning to feel and correct.
setup: Stand on one foot in its tripod, other knee softly lifted
Find a fixed point to look at
Let the arch and ankle make tiny corrections to stay centered
Progress by closing the eyes
cues: Hold the foot in a locked arch (hyperarch) — a quiet, domed tripod, not clawing toes
Quiet the sway — feel the corrections get smaller
Knee soft, hips level

name: Banded clamshell
description: Side-lying hip external rotation against a light band — direct glute-medius/rotator activation to feed knee control from above.
setup: Lie on your side, knees bent, band above the knees, hips stacked
Keep the feet together and the pelvis still
Open the top knee by rotating the hip, without rolling the pelvis back
Lower under control
cues: The pelvis must not rock backward — isolate the hip
Feel it in the side of the glute, not the low back
Pause at the top of each rep

name: Side-lying hip abduction
description: Raising the top leg straight up in side-lying to load the glute medius through range — the abductor strength that resists the knee caving in on landing.
setup: Lie on your side, bottom leg bent, top leg straight and in line with the body
Turn the top toes slightly down toward the floor
Raise the straight top leg toward the ceiling
Lower slowly without letting the hip roll
cues: Lead with the heel, toe slightly down — targets glute medius
Keep the leg slightly behind the body, not drifting forward
No rolling back to cheat height

name: Lateral band walk
description: Stepping sideways against a light band in a quarter-squat — glute-medius under a standing, closed-chain load with the knees driving out.

Step one foot out to the side, staying low
Bring the trailing foot in only partway so the band stays tensioned
Walk a set number of steps each direction
cues: Knees drive out against the band the whole time — never let them cave
Stay low and level; don't bob up and down
Feet point straight ahead

name: Copenhagen adduction (ball)
description: A side-plank with the top leg resting on the ball, lifting the bottom leg to it — the strongest adductor builder there is, scaled by lever length. No weights needed.
setup: Side-plank on a forearm, top leg's shin or foot resting on the ball
Start easy: keep the bottom knee bent and down (short lever)
Lift the hips so the body is straight, squeezing the bottom leg up toward the ball
Progress by straightening the bottom leg (long lever)
cues: Adductor of the down leg does the work — feel the inner thigh
Body stays in one straight line, hips high
Start with the short-lever (bent knee) version and earn the long lever

name: Adductor ball squeeze
description: Squeezing the ball between the knees in a bridge — an isometric adductor and deep-core connection that also stabilizes the pelvis.
setup: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat, the ball between the knees
Squeeze the ball firmly with both knees
Hold the squeeze and lift into a glute bridge
Keep squeezing throughout the hold
cues: Inner thighs and deep core switch on together
Ribs down, no arching the low back
Constant squeeze — don't let the ball relax

description: A held bridge that wakes the glutes and teaches hip extension driven by the glute, not the low back — the reciprocal partner that quiets an overactive psoas.

Drive through the heels and lift the hips to a straight knee-hip-shoulder line
Squeeze the glutes hard; keep the ribs down
Hold, then lower slowly
cues: If you feel it in the hamstrings or low back, walk the feet slightly out

Drive one knee up toward the chest, holding briefly at the top
Return and switch sides without dropping the hips

Return to tall by squeezing the glute

description: Low, fast hops off a locked-arch foot — the very first rung of the plyo ladder. Building the reactive stiffness the sport needs at minimal knee cost, with the HFT drive: the heel rises by rolling the hips forward, not by pressing down through the calf.

name: Single-leg pogo (low)
description: Low single-leg pogo hops — the step up to unilateral reactive stiffness and symmetry, only after double-leg work is clean and symptom-free.
setup: Balance on one foot, tall, knee soft
Perform small, fast hops in place on that foot
Land forefoot-first with a quiet, quick rebound
Keep the hip and knee stacked over the foot
cues: Knee must stay over the foot on every landing — no cave-in
Light and quick; keep amplitude low
Stop the set the moment landings lose control

name: Curb drop to stick
description: Stepping off a curb and sticking a soft, silent two-foot landing — teaching absorption before generation. The safe front door to impact.
setup: Stand on a curb or low step
Step off (don't jump) and land on both feet at once
Absorb by bending the ankles, knees, and hips together
Stick and hold the landing dead still for a beat
cues: Silent landing — soft and quiet means good absorption
Knees track out over the feet as you catch; never let them cave
Stick and freeze; own the landing before the next rep

name: Single-leg landing stick
description: A small hop landing and sticking on one leg — single-leg absorption and knee control, the landing quality that gates a return to cutting.
setup: Stand on one leg, small hop forward or to the side
Land on that same foot and immediately stick it
Absorb through ankle, knee, and hip; free leg tucked for balance
Hold the landing still for a full beat before the next rep
cues: Soft, silent, and stuck — the knee stays over the foot
No wobble or inward dive on the catch
Quality over quantity — end the set if control slips

name: Lateral bound to stick
description: A controlled sideways push-off, landing and sticking on the outside leg — the multidirectional, court-specific expression of everything below it. Amplitude earned over time.
setup: Start on one leg, sink slightly, and push off sideways
Land on the opposite (outside) leg and stick it
Absorb the landing with the knee tracking over the foot
Pause, balanced, then bound back the other way
cues: Stick each landing before returning — control the direction change
Outside knee stays stacked over the foot on the catch
Start with small distance; grow it only as landings stay silent and stable

name: Side plank
description: The lateral-chain isometric — trains the obliques and glute medius to keep the pelvis level, the trunk half of keeping the knee stacked.
setup: Lie on your side, forearm under the shoulder, legs stacked or staggered
Lift the hips so the body is one straight line
Stack the top hip directly over the bottom
Hold; drop the knee to the floor to regress
cues: Hips high and level — don't let the bottom hip sag
Long line from head to feet
Press the down-side floor away through the forearm

name: Pallof press (band)
description: Pressing a band straight out while it tries to twist you — an anti-rotation isometric that teaches the trunk to resist the forces of cutting and landing.
setup: Anchor the band at chest height to the side, hold it at the sternum
Stand tall in an athletic stance, side-on to the anchor
Press the hands straight out and resist the band's pull to rotate you
Hold, then return; the band never wins the twist
cues: Stay square — the whole job is refusing to rotate
Brace the trunk and squeeze the glutes
Ribs down, breathe through the hold

name: Bird dog
description: From all fours, extending opposite arm and leg while keeping the trunk perfectly still — cross-body coordination and anti-rotation that ties the hips and shoulders together.
setup: Start on hands and knees, spine neutral, core braced
Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back to a long line
Keep the hips and shoulders square to the floor
Return under control and switch sides
cues: No twisting — a glass of water on the low back wouldn't spill
Reach long rather than high; squeeze the extending glute
Slow and deliberate on both the reach and the return

name: Crocodile breathing
description: Prone diaphragmatic breathing to down-regulate — sets a calm baseline to open the session or close it, so the day isn't one long brace.
setup: Lie face down, forehead on stacked hands, feet relaxed
Inhale into the belly so it presses into the floor and the low back rises
Exhale slowly through the nose and let the belly soften
Repeat with a long, unhurried rhythm
cues: Feel the breath in the back and sides of the torso, not the chest
Exhale roughly twice as long as the inhale
Let global muscle tension drain out on each breath

name: Long-line active reach
description: An active down-dog-style reach that loads the posterior line gently end-to-end — a moving decompression for the foot-to-glute chain, not a passive hold.
setup: From hands and feet, press the hips up and back into an inverted V
Reach the heels toward the floor, one at a time (pedal the feet)
Lengthen the spine by pushing the floor away
Keep gently moving rather than hanging in one position
cues: Pedal the heels to load calves and hamstrings alternately
Long spine — push the ground away through the hands
Active and breathing, not a limp stretch

name: Figure-4 glute opener
description: A brief seated or supine figure-4 to release the deep hip rotators after the session — kept short and gentle as a cool-down, not a mobility session in itself.
setup: Lie on your back, cross one ankle over the opposite knee (figure-4)
Reach through and gently draw the far thigh toward the chest
Feel the opening in the back of the crossed hip
Breathe and ease into it, then switch sides
cues: Gentle — this is a cool-down, not a max stretch
Keep the crossed-leg foot flexed to protect the knee
Relax the head and shoulders down
